title: status and snapshot read unbounded direct-child files before any cap

attack_path_facts.title: status and snapshot read unbounded direct-child files before any cap
attack_steps: A lower-trust content contributor places a very large or sparse regular direct-child file in a scope the victim uses.
The victim runs status or snapshot on that scope.
The working-tree builder accepts the file through the type, name, and exclusion filters and calls fs::read before applying any byte ceiling.
The victim process allocates and reads attacker-sized bytes; snapshot can additionally copy them into the archive, causing command failure or substantial local resource pressure.
assumptions: The selected scope is shared, supplied, or otherwise writable by a lower-trust content contributor.
The hostile file is a direct regular child and is not explicitly excluded.
The victim invokes a routine status or snapshot command.
attack_path_facts.context: KCS has no listener; this is a filesystem-mediated availability path. Impact crosses from lower-trust scope content into the victim KCS process, but remains local, recoverable, and limited to the selected workflow.
attack_path_facts.in_scope: yes; untrusted direct-child files and bounded local processing are explicit threat-model surfaces under I6 and I12
attack_path_facts.exposure: not public; reachable through local CLI processing of an adopted or shared scope
attack_path_facts.identity: KCS runs as the victim OS user with that user's filesystem and memory limits; the attacker needs no KCS or OS-administrator identity
attack_path_facts.cross_boundary: yes; lower-trust file size crosses the scope-content boundary into victim-process memory, I/O, and archive storage
attack_path_facts.preconditions: plausible: control one included direct-child file and wait for the operator to run status or snapshot; sparse files can make the logical-size amplification inexpensive
attack_path_facts.attacker_control: yes; the lower-trust contributor controls the included file's logical size and bytes
attack_path_facts.category: resource consumption / local denial of service (CWE-400, CWE-770)
mitigations: Subdirectories, symlinks observed at enumeration, non-regular entries, and explicit exclusions are skipped.
Status does not persist the bytes and snapshot holds the store lock.
The operator can remove the hostile file and retry.
attack_path_facts.auth_scope: internal-only; local filesystem and CLI surface with no network authentication boundary
attack_path_facts.impact_surface: runtime memory and I/O; snapshot also affects archive disk usage
attack_path_facts.target_reach: one KCS process and selected scope per invocation
counterevidence: The later effective_max_input_bytes control applies only to adapter processing and does not protect status or snapshot.
The command is recoverable after removing the file and does not create a confidentiality or authorization bypass.
blindspots: No large or sparse-file runtime measurement was retained; actual failure thresholds depend on host limits.
attack_path_facts.rationale: A realistic lower-trust scope contributor can deterministically reach a victim resource sink through routine commands, so self-only suppression does not apply. The required matrix maps medium impact plus high likelihood to medium.
